lessons.title: The same bytes, two integer views
lessons.ask: Do the bytes change when we choose a different byte order?
lessons.predict: Predict both u16 values before running the program.
lessons.live_edit: Start with the little-endian line; add the big-endian conversion and print it.
lessons.explain: u8 is one byte. [u8; 2] fixes the length in the type. &[u8] borrows a view. u16 is a chosen two-byte interpretation; the original meaning remains unknown.
lessons.find: New workshop investigation: select record 3, then record 4. Change the endian selector in Harness Insight. The evidence bytes stay 34 12.
lessons.answer: Little endian gives 4660; big endian gives 13330. Neither proves a firmware field type.
lessons.stdout:
Synthetic bytes: [34, 12]
little-endian u16: 4660
big-endian u16: 13330
Intended meaning: unknown

lessons.title: Give the observation an owner
lessons.ask: What must we retain so another person can check this observation?
lessons.predict: Name a source location, the bytes and a description.
lessons.live_edit: Fill the three Observation fields. Change only its description and rerun.
lessons.explain: A struct keeps related fields together. Vec<u8> owns a growable sequence. String owns text. This is the application's actual Observation type, not a recovered target struct.
lessons.find: Record 3 shows its file offset and bytes. Rust type annotations under View identify the host Observation type.
lessons.answer: The description can change without changing the observed bytes. A meaningful source reference matters more than a plausible number.
lessons.stdout:
file+0x0: [34, 12]
Synthetic teaching bytes / 2 bytes
Vec<u8> owns the bytes; String owns the description.

lessons.title: Name the kind of claim
lessons.ask: Should a question, an observation and an explanation carry the same fields?
lessons.predict: Assign a record kind to each step in the six-card teaching graph.
lessons.live_edit: Write the Question, Observation and Explanation match arms, then inspect the remaining variants.
lessons.explain: An enum represents alternatives. A match makes handling those alternatives explicit. RecordData separates observations, explanations and open questions. The wildcard here covers additional implemented variants, not unknown evidence.
lessons.find: Graph card kind labels and the terminal header use the same RecordData. Record 5 is an Unknown carrying a question plan; record 6 is another Question.
lessons.answer: The value 4660 belongs to an explanation. It cannot be relabeled as an observation merely because a model repeats it.
lessons.stdout:
#1 question
#2 probe
#3 observation
#4 explanation
#5 unknown
#6 question

lessons.title: Absence and failure are different
lessons.ask: Is an unknown destination the same as a failed two-byte read?
lessons.predict: Predict the full read, truncated read and destination outcomes.
lessons.live_edit: Change the read from &bytes to &bytes[..1], then add Option<MappedAddress> = None.
lessons.explain: Option<T> distinguishes Some(value) from None. Result<T, E> distinguishes Ok(value) from Err(reason). Missing information is not the number zero. An operation can succeed while its semantic meaning remains unknown.
lessons.find: Select the final byte in the workshop inspector: the u16 view becomes unavailable. Unmapped addresses say unresolved. Failed or cancelled tool receipts remain separate from evidence.
lessons.answer: The full read is Ok(4660). The short read is Err. None means no destination has been supplied; it is not address 0.
lessons.stdout:
Two bytes: Ok(4660)
One byte: Err("Two bytes are required")
Destination: unknown; no address was invented

lessons.title: Borrow data; distinguish coordinates
lessons.ask: Can a declared CPU address be passed directly to a file reader?
lessons.predict: Predict whether wrong_coordinate.rs compiles, and whether the Vec remains usable after a borrowed read.
lessons.live_edit: Borrow &bytes, run the intentional coordinate error, then replace the argument with FileOffset(0).
lessons.explain: &[u8] lets a function read without taking ownership. FileOffset and MappedAddress wrap the same numeric representation but have different Rust types. A checked mapping establishes a relationship between spaces; changing the wrapper name does not.
lessons.find: Harness Insight distinguishes file+, image offsets and declared addresses. In the synthetic fixture the mapped address is unresolved. The later V15 module shows the actual source map.
lessons.answer: The compiler reports E0308: expected FileOffset, found MappedAddress. For this two-byte buffer, FileOffset(0) is valid. Do not fix the error by copying a CPU address into a file offset.
lessons.stdout:
Borrowed 2 bytes
Owner still has: [34, 12]
File read: Ok(4660)
Declared address: 0x02000120
These coordinates need a checked map, not a cast.

lessons.title: Connect an explanation to evidence
lessons.ask: What lets someone challenge an explanation after the model has stopped?
lessons.predict: Find the observation ID cited by record 4 and state a limitation.
lessons.live_edit: Resolve the evidence ID, print its title, then print the explanation's uncertainty and next step.
lessons.explain: RecordId names a record in one investigation. ObservationId resolves only to an evidence role. Result and ? propagate a failed validation. A valid citation makes a claim traceable, but does not prove the claim is true.
lessons.find: Select explanation 4 and follow evidence 3. Open the saved synthetic replay to see an analyst correction retained alongside the original explanation.
lessons.answer: Record 4 cites observation 3. The bytes support a chosen integer view; they do not establish intended meaning. A format declaration or controlled example is a useful next probe.
lessons.stdout:
#4 / Derived
Evidence #3: Two bytes: 34 12
Explanation: u16::from_le_bytes([0x34, 0x12]) yields 4660 (0x1234). This is a reproducible interpretation of the bytes.
Limitation: We have not established that the original author intended an integer, or what the value represents. These are synthetic teaching bytes, not FM-1 evidence.
Next: Find a format declaration or a controlled example that assigns meaning to this field.
